evals.prompt: Làm màn hình quản lý API keys gồm list, search, create/edit và delete. App đang dùng tiếng Nhật. Bám theo style hiện tại, đừng hỏi nhiều.
evals.expected_output: Loads upstream frontend-design and project DESIGN.md or creates it from existing evidence, inspects sibling flows, implements bounded table navigation, IME-safe debounced clearable search, masked key fields, complete Japanese locale/copy, app dialog for deletion, consistent save-back-to-list behavior, and verifies all states.

evals.prompt: Build the B1 create screen to match our existing A1 flow. Saving A1 returns to list A with a toast. Add password and notes fields, and polish interactions.
evals.expected_output: Infers B1 should return to list B, reads the design context, reuses shared feedback/navigation patterns, masks password with reveal control, disables textarea resize with adequate sizing, disables native validation UI, and includes hover/focus/busy/error behavior without unnecessary questions.

evals.prompt: Review and fix this React admin table. It loads all records, uses window.confirm for delete, the search fires on every key, rows are clickable divs, and loading changes the page width.
evals.expected_output: Finds and fixes production violations through existing/shared primitives: dataset navigation decision, app-owned accessible confirmation, debounced cancelable IME-safe search with clear control, semantic row navigation/actions, responsive overflow, scrollbar/layout stability, state coverage, and regression verification.

evals.prompt: Create a one-page experimental marketing hero with no forms, tables, accounts, or app workflows. Make it visually unforgettable.
evals.expected_output: The premium skill composes upstream visual design and applies accessibility/stability, but does not force CRUD contracts or create durable application artifacts for a throwaway isolated marketing surface unless the repository already uses them.

evals.prompt: Start a new multi-screen operations SaaS from this short business brief. Make the dashboard and user-management foundation; choose the design direction yourself.
evals.expected_output: Loads frontend-design, derives a concrete product-register North Star and anti-references, proactively creates a valid root DESIGN.md and UX-CONTRACT.md, establishes implementable tokens and shared primitives, avoids generic adjectives/default aesthetics, and lints/verifies the design context.

evals.prompt: Standardize billing settings in this mature 120-screen app. There is no DESIGN.md, four Button families and three dialog/toast systems coexist, but the app has a theme package and Storybook. Do not big-bang redesign or break releases.
evals.expected_output: Uses scan mode to document rather than rebrand the existing identity, traces canonical runtime token ownership into DESIGN.md, inventories duplicate primitives and behavior drift in one migration ledger, selects targets by safety rather than popularity, hardens adapters/shared primitives, prioritizes destructive billing flows, defines rollout/rollback and legacy-removal gates, and avoids an unreviewable 120-screen rewrite.

evals.prompt: Implement a Japanese onboarding wizard with company autocomplete, establishment date range, logo/document upload, a review step, and resumable draft saving.
evals.expected_output: Implements accessible IME-safe combobox, localized date/range semantics, picker-accessible upload with validation/progress/retry, stable multi-step navigation and per-step validation, explicit draft local/sync/saved/failed states, Japanese calendar/timezone decisions, and full keyboard/error/offline verification.

evals.prompt: Make this audit-records screen work on mobile. It has 14 columns, bulk revoke, expandable details, tabs, breadcrumbs, a desktop sidebar, and long IDs.
evals.expected_output: Chooses a responsive table strategy from comparison needs without silently dropping data, keeps selection scope and dangerous bulk count exact, implements accessible row disclosure/tabs/breadcrumbs, transforms sidebar to a focus-managed drawer, exposes full truncated IDs without hover-only access, and preserves route/filter/focus state.

evals.prompt: Make status toggles instant and add autosave to profile editing. Users often work in two tabs and their session can expire.
evals.expected_output: Classifies optimistic eligibility, adds pending/rollback/reconciliation and idempotency, defines truthful autosave and draft recovery, prevents multi-tab/newer-version overwrites, preserves safe work through session expiry/re-auth, and tests uncertain completion rather than only happy paths.

evals.prompt: Build a long-running CSV import: upload, mapping, background processing, progress, partial failures, activity log, notification count, and offline reconnect.
evals.expected_output: Implements safe accessible upload and mapping, server-confirmed background job creation, truthful determinate/staged progress with leave-and-return path, partial success recovery, semantic audit timeline/timezone, stable accessible badge count, degraded connectivity banner, bounded retries and reconnect revalidation.

evals.prompt: Add keyboard shortcuts, a Ctrl+K command palette, a right-click row menu, sortable drag handles, accordion help, and a dual range slider. Everything must be keyboard accessible.
evals.expected_output: Treats shortcuts/context menu as conditional enhancements, avoids browser/IME/input conflicts, provides visible menu and non-drag alternatives, implements complete combobox/menu/accordion/slider semantics and focus restoration, respects reduced motion, and verifies keyboard-only and screen-reader behavior.

evals.prompt: Add dark mode and change our app-wide button radius and accent color. DESIGN.md, CSS variables, Tailwind config and ThemeProvider currently duplicate values. Update shared screens without introducing token drift.
evals.expected_output: Reads existing DESIGN.md, chooses and documents one token ownership model, maps DESIGN paths through generated or canonical CSS variables into Tailwind/ThemeProvider adapters and shared components, removes independent duplicate literals, preserves semantic intent and contrast across themes, runs DESIGN.md lint/diff plus token drift checks, and performs representative cross-theme state/visual regression instead of patching screens individually.

evals.prompt: Add a slide-in cart drawer with staggered item entrance and a confirmation dialog. The dialog should scale in on open and fade out on close. Respect reduced motion.
evals.expected_output: Implements drawer slide-in with cubic-bezier 250ms, staggered list items at 50ms delay each, dialog spring entrance (scale 1.05 to 1), opacity-only exit at 150ms, reduced motion fallback (opacity only, no transform), and AnimatePresence for exit animations. Does not animate decorative elements.

evals.prompt: Build a user profile edit form with React Hook Form + Zod (or Formik + Yup), email and password fields. Show a common error banner for server errors and inline field errors. The form uses Japanese error messages.
evals.expected_output: Uses either Formik+Yup or React Hook Form+Zod for form state and validation. Has separate common error banner via useState, server error to field mapping (setFieldError/setError), post-submit recovery (clear on edit), and novalidate/noValidate. Japanese messages explain what is wrong and how to fix. Submit button shows busy state, prevents double submit, preserves values on server error.

evals.prompt: Review this existing app: DESIGN.md says 'flat surfaces at rest' but all cards have box-shadow. It says 'pill radius buttons' but the Button component uses 8px radius. It says 'no bold body text' but section titles use semibold. What do you recommend?
evals.expected_output: Produces a structured drift report table (Rule, Evidence, Verdict, Action). Classifies each discrepancy as intentional evolution (update DESIGN.md), unintentional drift (fix code), or ambiguous (ask user). Does not silently rewrite DESIGN.md. Does not propose big-bang redesign. Records actions: some DESIGN.md updates, some component fixes, one question for the user.

evals.prompt: Migrate this project's tokens from a Tailwind v3 config file to v4 @theme inline. DESIGN.md, old tailwind.config.ts, and CSS :root currently duplicate values. Keep the DESIGN.md as the authoring layer.
evals.expected_output: Reads existing DESIGN.md and tailwind.config.ts. Chooses ownership model (DESIGN.md generates → @theme inline). Creates the @theme inline block from exported DESIGN.md values. Removes duplicate tailwind.config.ts. Maps all component utilities from old config classes to new @theme variables. Runs designmd lint + diff. Verifies no broken utility classes in components.

evals.prompt: Add a high-contrast theme to this app. The existing DESIGN.md defines light and dark themes via CSS variables. Keep semantic token names unchanged; only their values change per theme. Ensure WCAG contrast in all three themes.
evals.expected_output: Reads existing DESIGN.md and CSS theme variables. Adds a .high-contrast selector overriding only semantic tokens, not component styles. Verifies color contrast ratios in each theme using tooling or computed values. Updates DESIGN.md theme section to document the third theme. Does not duplicate component styles per theme — relies on CSS variable remapping.

evals.prompt: Standardize notifications across a 200-screen app. Currently: 3 toast libraries (react-toastify, sonner, custom), 2 dialog systems (shadcn + custom), and 4 banner styles. Prioritize destructive and billing flows.
evals.expected_output: Inventories all notification surfaces and classifies by severity (toast, dialog, banner). Selects one canonical toast/dialog/banner primitive. Hardens the selected components with compatibility layer for existing callers. Migrates destructive and billing workflows first (highest risk). Defines rollout gates: all new code uses canonical, legacy removed after 2 weeks zero-defect. Creates migration ledger with rollback criteria.

evals.prompt: Implement a Japanese registration form that only accepts corporate email addresses (reject gmail.com, yahoo.co.jp, etc.). Validate with regex, show localized error, and handle the common exclusion pattern.
evals.expected_output: Implements email field with real-time regex exclusion of consumer email providers. Shows Japanese error message listing excluded domains. Uses Yup test() for validationSchema and additional client pre-check before submit. Common error banner for server validation and inline field error for immediate rejection. Novalidate on form. Tested with both allowed and blocked addresses.

evals.prompt: Write a Python script to parse JSON logs and extract error rates by service. Output a summary table. No UI needed.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT activate frontend-design or frontend-design-premium. The task is backend-only data processing with no UI. The agent should decline to apply UI design context or production contracts, and write only the Python script.

evals.prompt: Add a destructive delete button to this user row. When clicked, show a confirmation dialog. The delete is irreversible. The async operation should keep the dialog open during loading.
evals.expected_output: Uses app-owned AlertDialog with destructive intent styling (danger variant, red). Dialog titles the action, names the user, describes consequence ('irreversible'). Cancel button gets initial focus. Async mutation keeps dialog open with loading spinner; error stays in dialog with retry; success closes dialog and shows toast. Button uses the destructive verb ('Delete', not 'OK').

evals.prompt: Draft a UX-CONTRACT.md for a multi-step checkout flow. Include save/cancel behavior, validation strategy, destructive actions, async resilience, and locale policy.
evals.expected_output: Creates a UX-CONTRACT.md following the template. Documents create/edit/delete flow behaviors, server pagination default, common error + inline validation, destructive confirm with danger intent, timeout/session handling, and Japanese locale. Does NOT duplicate visual tokens from DESIGN.md.

evals.prompt: Review and fix permission UX on this analysis detail page. Viewers should understand why Delete/Edit are unavailable, Billing should not appear for roles that never pay, clipboard copy must be accessible, and direct navigation to admin settings must not look like a missing page.
evals.expected_output: Reads references/permission-ui.md. Chooses hide vs disable vs 403 correctly: hide Billing for irrelevant roles; show Edit/Delete disabled with an accessible why explanation (not title-only); replace window.confirm with app-owned dialog for admins; implement copy control with changing accessible label and failure feedback; use a dedicated 403/access-denied route for forbidden deep links instead of 404; notes server-side auth remains the source of truth.

evals.prompt: Fix overlay stacking on this job detail screen. A drawer, confirm dialog, and toast overlap incorrectly; z-index values are magic numbers; focus and Escape behavior are missing.
evals.expected_output: Reads references/layer-contract.md. Introduces a documented z-index scale via CSS variables (no 9999). Orders layers: backdrop < dialog above drawer; toast always topmost. Adds focus trap, Escape=Cancel, inert/aria-hidden background, and focus restoration. Dialog opened from drawer stacks above the drawer. Toast uses a live region and is never obscured.

evals.prompt: Implement a user-deactivation flow for an admin panel. The ADR says deactivation is reversible for 30 days and only Owners can perform it. The existing code has a hard-delete endpoint. There is no permission-policy document. Decide what to build and document the rationale.
evals.expected_output: Discovers ADR and domain evidence before visual planning. Distinguishes authoritative policy (ADR: reversible deactivation, Owner-only) from implementation evidence (hard-delete endpoint). Acknowledges ADR is already authoritative for the Owner-only rule (no escalation needed for permission). Surfaces the conflict between ADR lifecycle (reversible deactivation) and existing code (hard-delete endpoint). Records source references in UX-CONTRACT.md without copying business policy. Does not ask the user about decisions already settled by authoritative evidence.

evals.prompt: Design a billing settings page for an existing SaaS. The product has ADR-007 describing subscription lifecycle (trial→active→expired→cancelled). The API contract exposes an idempotent cancellation endpoint. There is no billing-spec document. Handle the cancel-subscription workflow.
evals.expected_output: Discovers ADR-007 and the API contract before designing. Recognises billing/payment as a high-risk category that must not use generic defaults. Reads ADR lifecycle transitions and API idempotency guarantees. Resolves that cancellation is idempotent and server-confirmed (pessimistic mutation). Does not implement optimistic cancellation. Records the authoritative source references in UX-CONTRACT.md (ADR-007, API contract path) rather than duplicating the subscription rules. Treats missing billing-spec as an escalated gap.

evals.prompt: Build a Japan-market consumer ecommerce checkout in Japanese. Product policy defines inventory reservation and payment idempotency, but there is no maintained source for tax wording, recurring-payment disclosure, returns, or the final-order confirmation requirements.
evals.expected_output: Separates Japan market from ja-JP locale, loads the market/content/visual/localization packs and the regulated-flow pack, uses the known inventory/idempotency contracts, and explicitly escalates every missing tax/legal/returns/subscription authority instead of inventing copy. The design preserves review, edit, and final commitment as distinct states and names the exact evidence still required.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it treats ja-JP formatting as legal compliance, guesses tax/returns/subscription language, or makes the review CTA place the order.

evals.prompt: Fix this Japanese profile editor. Autosave, Enter-to-submit, Ctrl+K, character counting, and company autocomplete all react during IME composition, and stale suggestions can replace a newer value.
evals.expected_output: Implements a shared composition-aware input contract across autosave, submit, shortcuts, counters, autocomplete, and remote requests; dispatches the final value once after composition; cancels or ignores stale responses; and adds event-level tests that prove zero side effects while composing and the correct final side effect after compositionend.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if Japanese labels or comments say IME-safe while onChange, Enter, autosave, shortcuts, counters, or stale responses still consume incomplete composition.

evals.prompt: Create a Japanese public-service application flow for older adults. It must work at 200% zoom, use clear Japanese guidance, and support a high-accessibility review process.
evals.expected_output: Grounds density and guidance in older-adult/public-service evidence, uses readable Japanese typography and explicit correction guidance, verifies Japanese screen-reader output and WCAG 2.2 AA plus applicable JIS X 8341-3-oriented checks, and records native-domain copy review and representative user testing as release evidence rather than claiming readiness from source inspection.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it uses small dense text because Japanese sites are assumed dense, or claims accessibility from WCAG prose without Japanese assistive-technology evidence.

evals.prompt: Design an account-opening service used in Japan by Japanese users and foreign residents. The primary UI is Japanese with English assistance; legal names may use Kanji, kana, Latin script, middle names, or one name.
evals.expected_output: Records audience and bilingual policy separately from locale, provides flexible legal/display/readings data paths without forcing a two-field Kanji model, supports international phone/address needs alongside Japanese order, and routes unresolved identity requirements to the authoritative domain owner. Japanese and English assistance remain semantically aligned and accessible.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if every person is forced into surname/given-name Kanji plus Katakana-only furigana, or if English support bypasses Japan-market identity rules.

evals.prompt: Audit a Japanese B2B operations dashboard with long company names, mixed Kanji/Latin identifiers, dense tables, and comparison-heavy daily work. Improve it without making it consumer-spacious or stereotypically cluttered.
evals.expected_output: Derives density from comparison frequency and expert workflow, defines separate prose/control/dense-data typography, checks Japanese-capable fallback, mixed-script metrics, full-value access, focus and targets, 200% zoom, and ja-JP visual regression. It preserves useful density while rejecting both generic airy SaaS minimalism and Japan-equals-clutter assumptions.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if density is chosen from cultural shorthand, important values become hover-only, or Japanese fallback and zoom are not rendered.

evals.prompt: Implement a Japan registration form covering personal and corporate names, furigana, postal-code address suggestions, domestic/international phones, full-/half-width input, fiscal year, and Japanese IME. Frontend and backend normalization rules are not yet aligned.
evals.expected_output: Uses an explicit data contract, keeps postal suggestions editable, handles corporate prefix/suffix and legitimate foreign-name/readings cases, distinguishes display/source values from normalization keys, exercises IME outside search, and escalates the frontend/backend normalization mismatch instead of silently normalizing only the client.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it uses one rigid phone/furigana regex, locks auto-filled addresses, rewrites legal names, or hides a client/backend normalization mismatch.

evals.prompt: Review Japanese validation, empty, confirmation, toast, and button copy across a checkout. The interface has translated OK buttons, mixed お客様/ユーザー terminology, cold schema errors, and English aria-labels.
evals.expected_output: Chooses and documents a consistent Japanese register and glossary, replaces generic actions with outcome-specific verbs, differentiates review from commitment, provides field-specific recovery, localizes accessible names, and requires native Japanese domain review for critical copy. It does not treat Japanese-character presence or machine translation as proof of naturalness.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if visible headings are Japanese but actions, errors, aria-labels, emails, or library defaults leak English or use generic OK.

evals.prompt: Make this global SaaS landing page feel Japanese for a Tokyo launch. Add sakura, a red sun, brush lettering, anime accents, Zen whitespace, and denser text so Japanese visitors trust it.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the ungrounded stereotype brief, asks for or derives evidence from the actual audience, sector, brand, and comparable Japanese products, and proposes a Japan-market content/typography/trust direction without forcing application contracts. Cultural motifs are used only if approved brand or campaign evidence supports them.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it implements any requested cultural shorthand merely to appear Japanese.

evals.prompt: Build an English-language merchant dashboard that operates only in Japan. It handles Japanese corporate names, addresses, JPY settlement, consumption-tax fields, and domestic support workflows.
evals.expected_output: Routes Japan-market and data contracts despite the non-ja UI, does not force Japanese copy, applies Japanese corporate/address/currency behavior where authoritative, and escalates tax/invoice/support rules that lack maintained domain sources. Market and locale remain separate in DESIGN.md and UX-CONTRACT.md.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if locale=en causes Japan-market data/legal rules to be skipped or if English UI is silently translated.

evals.prompt: Add an APPI consent screen and cross-border data-transfer disclosure for a Japan service. There is no approved purpose-of-use copy, retention policy, transfer inventory, or legal owner sign-off.
evals.expected_output: Loads the regulated-flow authority gate, identifies every missing source and owner, and stops the affected legal-copy decision. It may design a clearly marked structural placeholder but must not invent consent, retention, transfer, or deletion policy or copy a GDPR cookie banner.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it writes definitive APPI copy, certifies compliance, or imports GDPR behavior without Japan-specific authority.

evals.prompt: Design a Japanese subscription purchase flow. The API contract defines payment idempotency, but renewal timing, cancellation policy, tax labels, returns, seller information, and required final-confirmation disclosures are unresolved.
evals.expected_output: Uses the API evidence only for payment behavior, escalates unresolved commerce and legal policy, preserves review/edit/final-commit boundaries, and defines failure, duplicate-submit, timeout, uncertain-completion, receipt, and support states without inventing subscription terms.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if one CTA both reviews and commits, or if missing policy is replaced by generic ecommerce defaults.

evals.prompt: Create a Japanese-language marketing page for a new B2B service. It has no forms or app workflows, but it needs credible Japanese copy, typography, line breaking, trust cues, and a native review plan.
evals.expected_output: Keeps upstream ownership of creative direction and avoids UX-CONTRACT/CRUD machinery, while still loading Japan market, Japanese content, and Japanese visual-layout guidance. It sets evidence-based register and trust cues, Japanese-capable type, kinsoku and mixed-script checks, long-copy responsive verification, and native review for high-traffic acquisition copy.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if the marketing register skips Japanese content/typography rules or if it is forced through application-only contracts.

evals.prompt: Fix this Japanese account-type select. The closed trigger has the intended border and width, but the opened option popup uses a thinner border and different width. Keep the control accessible and make the popup geometry part of the component contract.
evals.expected_output: Explicitly decides between a native select and an authored accessible Select/Listbox. Because popup geometry is a visual requirement, it replaces the native select with the project's maintained primitive, aligns the popup to the trigger, matches outer width within 1 CSS px, reuses border/radius/density tokens, portals with collision handling and bounded scrolling, preserves Japanese labels and form integration, and verifies the open popup in a real browser with keyboard, zoom, long-option, and viewport-edge cases.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it tries to style native option elements, claims CSS can guarantee the operating-system popup geometry, or checks only the closed trigger.

evals.prompt: Fix this Japanese order-date field. The closed field is on a Japanese page, but opening it shows August, English weekday abbreviations, Clear, and Today. Keep Gregorian dates, display YYYY/MM/DD, store an ISO date-only value, and make the open calendar consistently Japanese.
evals.expected_output: Explicitly decides between a native and authored date picker. Because the open calendar language is a product requirement, it replaces the native input with the project's maintained accessible date-picker primitive, loads the complete ja-JP locale pack, keeps Gregorian calendar semantics, separates YYYY/MM/DD display from ISO YYYY-MM-DD storage, localizes heading/weekdays/navigation/today/clear and accessible names, and verifies the open popup in a real browser with keyboard, pointer, Escape, focus restoration, zoom, short-viewport collision, bounded height, and scrolling.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it keeps native input[type=date] while claiming lang=ja guarantees the popup, checks only the closed value, leaves any owned calendar label in English, conflates YYYY/MM/DD display with ISO storage, or switches to imperial-era dates without a product requirement.

evals.prompt: Fix the scrollbar system in this component library. Existing tables look correct only when developers remember a ui-scroll-container class; this new overflow-x-auto table shows the browser-default gray scrollbar and native arrow buttons. Every product-owned scroll surface must automatically use the project theme.
evals.expected_output: Moves the tokenized scrollbar baseline into the application global stylesheet so new scroll containers require no opt-in class. Defines track, thumb, hover, active, width, WebKit-compatible selectors, Firefox scrollbar-color/scrollbar-width, and a forced-colors path. Keeps per-container classes only for explicit gutter/density exceptions, scopes styling to the app document rather than browser chrome or third-party frames, and verifies an unclassed overflow container plus the application root in a real browser using computed styles, screenshots, keyboard scrolling, and high-contrast coverage.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it merely adds the existing scrollbar class to this component, requires future overflow containers to opt in, hides the scrollbar, hardcodes colors outside the token system, or claims a source selector proves rendered behavior without testing an unclassed scroll surface.

evals.prompt: A Vue admin page has two tabs: a 50-column, 50,000-record table and a 20-field order form. Make only the table fill the remaining viewport and scroll internally without changing its footprint. The long form must remain naturally scrollable and fully reachable.
evals.expected_output: Assigns scroll ownership per tab panel instead of applying table sizing to the shared page shell. The table panel uses a bounded flex chain with min-height: 0 and an internal overflow region; pagination remains inside the table frame. The form panel keeps natural block height and document or content-area scrolling, with only the action bar optionally sticky. Switching tabs does not leave h-dvh, fixed height, or overflow:hidden clipping on the form. Verifies both tabs at short and tall viewports, 200% zoom, and with 10/20/50 table page sizes.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if h-dvh, fixed height, or overflow:hidden is applied to a shared ancestor merely to size the table; if the form body becomes internally fixed or clipped; if only the active table tab is verified; or if table and form are forced to share one scroll owner.

evals.prompt: Replace this Japanese customer autocomplete. It uses input[list] and datalist, but the product requires an authored popup width, border, localized empty/loading states, and consistent keyboard behavior across supported browsers.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes datalist as a browser-owned popup and replaces it with the project's maintained accessible Combobox/Autocomplete primitive. Preserves Japanese labels and form integration, uses IME-safe filtering, matches authored popup geometry, supports Arrow keys, Enter, Escape, focus restoration, empty/loading/error/disabled states, bounded scrolling, zoom, and viewport collision, and verifies the open popup in supported browsers.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it keeps input[list]/datalist while claiming option CSS controls the opened popup, hand-builds incomplete ARIA behavior, ignores IME composition, or verifies only the closed input.

evals.prompt: Audit this Tailwind-styled Japanese account select. It uses appearance-none and custom trigger borders, but the opened native option popup must match the authored geometry.
evals.expected_output: Detects appearance-none as native-chrome stripping rather than an authored popup. Makes the native-versus-authored decision explicit, uses the maintained accessible Select/Listbox when popup geometry is required, and verifies trigger/content width, borders, keyboard behavior, scrolling, zoom, and collision in a real browser.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if the audit searches only for appearance: none, treats appearance-none as sufficient popup styling, or checks only the closed native select.

evals.prompt: Fix Japanese scheduling controls that use native time, month, week, and datetime-local inputs. Their opened pickers show platform-owned English labels, but the product requires consistent Japanese popup UI.
evals.expected_output: Applies the native-versus-authored ownership decision to every sibling picker type, not only date. Uses maintained accessible date/time primitives where popup locale is product-owned, preserves typed storage semantics, loads complete ja-JP copy, and verifies visible/accessibility labels, keyboard and pointer interaction, Escape, focus restoration, zoom, and viewport collision.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it audits only input[type=date], assumes lang=ja controls native time/month/week/datetime-local popups, or changes display text without verifying the opened pickers.

evals.prompt: Fix this global scrollbar theme. Chromium looks branded because the stylesheet defines only ::-webkit-scrollbar rules, while Firefox still shows its browser default scrollbar.
evals.expected_output: Treats WebKit pseudo-elements as engine fallbacks and adds tokenized standards-based scrollbar-color and scrollbar-width to the global application baseline. Preserves thumb, track, hover, active, forced-colors behavior and verifies unclassed scroll surfaces in Chromium and Firefox.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it keeps a WebKit-only scrollbar contract, adds an opt-in class, hides the scrollbar, or claims Chromium evidence proves Firefox coverage.

evals.prompt: Audit a shared Vue tab shell after a table viewport change. The shell uses h-full/min-h-screen and CSS height: 100%, causing the sibling 20-field form to clip even though no h-dvh class is present.
evals.expected_output: Detects h-full, min-h-screen, percentage height, and viewport-unit variants as possible table-height leaks. Scopes the bounded flex/min-height chain to the table panel, restores natural-height or canonical application scrolling for the form, and verifies both tabs at short/tall viewports, 200% zoom, and 10/20/50 page sizes.
evals.negative_oracle: Fails if it searches only for h-dvh/100vh, leaves h-full/min-h-screen/height:100% on the shared shell, verifies only the table tab, or creates nested form scrolling.
